plan: Given the low private value of $3, my optimal strategy is to bid conservatively, as the cost of winning (the third-highest bid) could easily exceed my value. I expect others to bid closer to their values, potentially higher if they have high values. By bidding low, I minimize potential losses. I will bid $0.1 to ensure minimal loss if I win unexpectedly, as the value of the prize is unlikely to exceed the cost of winning.

Given my value of $24, I aim to bid slightly below it to balance winning probability and profit. Assuming others bid near their value, I estimate their bids could range between $20 and $30. By bidding $23.5, I increase my chances of winning while ensuring profit if the third-highest bid is significantly lower. This strategy maximizes profit potential by targeting a win without overpaying.

Given my value of $11, I want to bid just enough to potentially win while ensuring my profit margin remains positive. Assuming others bid close to their values, I should bid slightly above half my value to avoid overbidding. A bid of around $6 should be competitive without risking a negative profit.
